body:
Confirmed: every usefulness and safety threshold must be preregistered before final evaluation and run on a frozen, disjoint acceptance corpus.

Required evidence protocol:
1) Three non-overlapping sets: development/vendor bake-off; validation/tuning; final held-out acceptance. No utterance, paraphrase of the same claim, source document/version, speaker recording, or deck instance may cross splits.
2) Before unblinding acceptance results, freeze and hash: corpus manifest, audio/deck/source artifacts, expert labels and adjudication guide, semantic endpoints, answerable/unanswerable status, claim class, direct-grounding labels, network profile, cache state, sample size, thresholds, metric formulas, timeout/failure treatment, exclusions, and statistical analysis.
3) Pre-register the already agreed gates: e2e semantic-end->eligible-render p95 <=5s; top-3 direct usefulness >=80% on answerable events; abstention >=95% on unanswerable events; false-SUPPORT <=1%; critical numeric/date/entity publication errors =0; false-CONFLICT <=5%; audience gain/loss/distraction gates; approval-load gates; lease/retract/recovery/privacy gates.
4) Vendor/model/retriever selection and threshold tuning use only development/validation. Acceptance is a single formal run. A failed result cannot be repaired by relabelling, dropping cases, moving the clock, or selecting a favorable subset.
5) If a real defect is fixed after failure, version the product and preregistration, retire the exposed corpus from acceptance status, create a new disjoint held-out set, and report the prior failure. Do not repeatedly test against the same holdout.
6) Report all claim classes and failure modes, not only the aggregate; confidence intervals accompany rates. Critical-zero remains zero regardless of aggregate precision.

Remaining fork analysis:
No unresolved semantic or safety fork requires user choice for implementation planning. Safe defaults are available:
• Second-device Console is secure baseline for extend and mirror.
• Human approval is mandatory; teammate may be active controller, but that is a per-session role choice, not an architecture fork.
• LIVE_VERIFIED public path is supervised and feature-flagged off outside the pilot.
• High-impact medical/legal/financial claims are excluded.
• Dynamic cards use <=3s leases; on uncertainty, hide.
• CURATED_PREAPPROVED also hides on disconnect by default. Offline persistence is enabled only for a signed/versioned deck package with explicit rights/DLP/slide-binding/local-expiry policy; no user prompt may weaken this ad hoc.
• Automatic placement is off/non-blocking; manual placement is canonical.
• Separate public/private origins and narrow DTO/gateway are the safe initial deployment default; registrable-domain consolidation is a later evidence-backed optimization, not a user-facing fork.

One product-scope choice may require explicit sponsor/user confirmation only if they reject the application-derived default: whether guarded-pilot completion is allowed to stop at private live recommendations. Default ruling is NO—the stated application promises live recommendations traversing approval to public output, so full contract includes a supervised feature-flagged public path. If the sponsor wants private-only as final MVP, that is a formal scope change and should be acknowledged in writing.

Everything else is measurable implementation detail, not an interview question.
